/.title: Microbial Metallomics: Metals, Microbes & the Microbiome
/.description: Explore how microbes acquire, use, and transform metals. A sourced field guide to metal biology, the microbiome, nutritional immunity, methods, and researchers.

/science.title: Microbial Metallomics: Metal Homeostasis, Enzymes & Immunity
/science.description: How microbes acquire metals, deliver enzyme cofactors, avoid mismetallation, and compete with hosts. Explore the mechanisms and the research behind them.

/metals.title: Metals & Microbes: The Microbial Metallomics Atlas
/metals.description: Explore 62 sourced profiles covering 70 elements: microbial enzymes, metal resistance, transformation, host competition, and open research questions.

/start-here.title: Start Here: Metal Availability & the Microbiome
/start-here.description: A framework for microbial metallomics: follow chemical form, compartments, and host–microbial competition to connect metal measurements with biological function.

/metal-access.title: Metal Bioavailability: Host–Microbe Compartment Explorer
/metal-access.description: Follow zinc, iron, copper, and cobalt through host and microbial compartments. Compare established findings with connections that research still needs to test.

/metals/nickel.title: Nickel in Bacteria: Urease, Hydrogenases & Metal Trafficking
/metals/nickel.description: How microbes acquire and use nickel in urease, [NiFe]-hydrogenases, and glyoxalase I. Explore primary studies, host interactions, and open research questions.

/disease-signatures.title: Metallomic Signatures of Disease & Microbial Mechanisms
/disease-signatures.description: Explore disease metal signatures in dementia, colorectal cancer and pregnancy—and the experiments that could connect them to microbial mechanisms.

/library/dementia-lewy-bodies-brain-meta.title: Dementia Metal Signatures: Lewy Bodies, Alzheimer’s & PDD
/library/dementia-lewy-bodies-brain-meta.description: Dementia brain-metal signatures reveal regional copper loss and iron gain. A critical review connects these patterns to testable microbial-metallomics research.

/library/alzheimers-brain-copper-metallo.title: Alzheimer’s Brain Metals: Copper, Iron & Zinc Patterns
/library/alzheimers-brain-copper-metallo.description: Alzheimer’s brain copper loss and regional iron and zinc changes reveal a spatial disease signature—and define experiments for microbial metallomics.

/library/parkinsons-dementia-brain-metal.title: Parkinson’s Dementia: Regional Brain Metal Signatures
/library/parkinsons-dementia-brain-metal.description: Brain copper loss in Parkinson’s dementia overlaps Alzheimer’s but differs by region. What this signature enables for microbial metallomics research.

/library/spatial-metallomics-colorectal-.title: Colorectal Cancer: Spatial Metallomics & Microbial Niches
/library/spatial-metallomics-colorectal-.description: Colorectal cancer metal maps reveal distinct copper and iron neighborhoods. What they measured, and how to test microbial access, host response and disease.

/library/heavy-metals-obesity-pregnancy-.title: UPBEAT Maternal Metallomics: Serum Metals & Pregnancy
/library/heavy-metals-obesity-pregnancy-.description: UPBEAT links maternal manganese and phosphorus to later outcomes. What the evidence means, and how to test host and microbial metal handling.
